Palo Alto names former SoftBank executive Nikesh Arora CEO

By Reuters

June 1, 2018 3:34 PM PDT Updated June 1, 2018

 

FILE PHOTO: SoftBank Group Corp President and COO Nikesh Arora speaks during a special lecture of the SoftBank Academia in Tokyo, Japan October 22, 2015. REUTERS/Toru Hanai/File photo

(Reuters) - Cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks Inc said on Friday it named former SoftBank Group Corp <9984.T> president Nikesh Arora as chief executive officer and chairman.

Arora, 50, succeeds Mark McLaughlin, who has led the company for nearly seven years and has played a major role in its torrid pace of growth.

Under McLaughlin, the company's shares have jumped five-fold since its initial public offering in 2012.

"Over the course of several quarters, I have been discussing succession planning with the Board and I couldn't be more pleased that we have found a leader in Nikesh," said McLaughlin, who will become the vice chairman of Palo Alto board.

Arora, who was Google's highest paid executive in 2012, joined SoftBank in September 2014 to take charge of its overseas operations.

He stepped down from SoftBank in 2016 following differences between him and SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son over when he would replace Son as head of the group.

During his two years at the group, Arora had used an extensive contact book to make new investments, including in Indian online marketplace Snapdeal and ride-hailing service Ola.

Arora has also been credited with making SoftBank more disciplined about investment exits.

Palo Alto also reported third-quarter revenue of \$567.1 million £424.9 million), beating analysts' average estimate of \$546.1 million, according to Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S.

Shares of the company were up 2.6 percent at \$214.69 in extended trading. They have risen about 44 percent this year.

Reporting by Munsif Vengattil in Bengaluru; Editing by Anil D'Silva

ultimate.snippet:
# Nikesh Arora to Become CEO of Palo Alto Networks: ‘I Really Wanted to Be an Operator’
June 1, 2018, 7:08 PM ET
![Video Poster](https://content.fortune.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/placeholder_16x9.jpg?format=webp&w=1440&quality=75)
Nikesh Arora, a Silicon Valley fixture who helped build Google and then [did a brief and tumultuous stint](https://fortune.com/2016/06/25/nikesh-arora-interview/) as president of Masayoshi Son’s Softbank, has finally landed his CEO job. Arora will become head of [Palo Alto Networks](https://fortune.com/company/palo-alto-networks/) on June 6, [replacing Mark McLaughlin](https://fortune.com/2016/03/02/rsa-conference-palo-alto-networks-ceo-keynote/).
Arora told *Fortune* in an interview Friday that after the SoftBank experience, “I went through the process of thinking about what I would do next, and I really wanted to be an operator. I wanted it to be at a growth company in a growth business… And I wanted to make sure it was the right company with the right team. The more time I spent with Mark and the team [at Palo Alto Networks], the more I got excited. It’s a great culture, a fast growth company, and the opportunity is to continue to work with the team and scale and expand.”
